blocks.text: 1. Unrolling

blocks.alt: A recurrent cell unrolls into a chain of copies across time

blocks.text: Hidden State, the previous topic, explored the evolving summary carried forward at each step. Unrolling is a way of visualizing how a Recurrent Neural Network processes an entire sequence, explored throughout this topic.
It works by drawing the same recurrent step repeated once for every single time step, laid out in a line, a genuinely useful visualization technique covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Recurrent Connection
This connects back to the recurrent connection, already covered in Vanilla RNN. The recurrent connection genuinely loops the hidden state back into the network itself, already covered there.

This is a genuinely compact but somewhat abstract way of drawing the network, hard to trace step by step visually, exactly the limitation that Unrolling exists specifically to address throughout this topic.
3. The Core Idea

blocks.alt: A compact loop view is compared against an unrolled chain view

blocks.text: Unrolling's genuinely core idea connects back to the same set of weights, already covered in Vanilla RNN. Draw one genuinely separate copy of the network for each time step, all sharing the exact same weights.

This genuinely transforms the compact, looping diagram already covered in the previous section into a genuinely linear sequence of copies, one for each time step already covered throughout this module.

blocks.text: 4. The Benefit Of Visual Clarity

blocks.alt: Unrolling makes data flow easier to visualize

blocks.text: This connects back to Training Loops, already covered in the Training Deep Networks module. Unrolling genuinely makes the sequential flow of computation, already covered throughout this module, genuinely easy to trace visually.
This turns an abstract, looping diagram into a genuinely concrete, linear one, directly mirroring the step-by-step training loop structure already covered in that earlier topic.
5. Shared Weights Across Every Copy

blocks.alt: Copy 1 and copy 2 both use shared weights

blocks.text: This connects back to the same set of weights, already covered in Vanilla RNN. Every single unrolled copy genuinely uses the exact same weights, not genuinely separate ones, despite looking like separate networks in the diagram.
This is a genuinely important, easy-to-miss detail: unrolling is purely a genuinely visual technique, not a structural change, and no genuinely new parameters get introduced by drawing it this way.

blocks.title: warning
blocks.content: A genuinely common misconception treats each unrolled copy as having genuinely its own independent weights. Unrolling, already covered in this topic, is purely visual; the underlying weights, already covered in Vanilla RNN, remain genuinely shared throughout.

blocks.text: 6. The Connection To Computational Graphs

blocks.alt: An unrolled RNN forms a computational graph

blocks.text: This connects back to the computational graph, already covered in Backpropagation & Optimization. An unrolled Recurrent Neural Network genuinely becomes a specific kind of computational graph.

This directly enables standard Backpropagation, already covered, to be applied across the entire unrolled sequence, exactly the mechanism covered in complete depth in the very next topic of this module.
7. Sequence Length Determines Graph Size

blocks.alt: A short sequence is compared against a long sequence in graph size

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real practical consequence connects back to the variable-length challenge, already covered in Sequence Data. A genuinely longer sequence genuinely produces a genuinely longer unrolled graph, with genuinely more copies of the network.
This is a genuinely direct, real consequence of the unrolling technique already covered throughout this topic, with the graph's own size scaling directly with the sequence's own length.

blocks.text: 8. The Memory Cost Of Unrolling

This connects back to Mixed Precision Training's own hardware theme, already covered. Storing every single unrolled copy's own intermediate values genuinely costs genuinely more memory for genuinely longer sequences.
This is a genuinely real, practical cost directly tied to the length dependency already covered in the previous section, a genuinely honest consideration when working with very long sequences.
9. Recognizing Why Unrolling Is Genuinely A Useful Mental Model

blocks.alt: Understanding RNN data flow points toward visualizing it as an unrolled chain

blocks.text: This connects back to understanding how a Recurrent Neural Network actually processes a specific sequence, step by step. Unrolling, already covered in this topic, makes that flow genuinely concrete and easy to trace.

This connects forward to Backpropagation Through Time, covered in the very next topic, which genuinely relies on this exact picture. Understanding Unrolling first, already covered, is a genuinely necessary prerequisite.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates constructing an unrolled representation of a Recurrent Neural Network processing a short sequence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence = ["the", "cat", "sat"]
hidden_size = 4

W_input = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, 3)) * 0.1   # already covered as shared weights across every copy
W_hidden = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1

unrolled_steps = []
hidden_state = np.zeros(hidden_size)

for t, word in enumerate(sequence):
    x_t = rng.normal(size=3)  # already covered as a genuinely simplified input representation
    hidden_state = np.tanh(W_input @ x_t + W_hidden @ hidden_state)  # already covered as the core update rule
    unrolled_steps.append({"time_step": t, "word": word, "hidden_state": hidden_state.copy()})
    print(f"Unrolled copy {t}: word='{word}', hidden state={np.round(hidden_state, 3)}")

print(f"\nTotal unrolled copies (already covered as sequence length determining graph size): {len(unrolled_steps)}")
print("Every copy above used the exact same W_input and W_hidden, already covered as shared weights across every copy in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example produces one unrolled copy per word in the sequence, all sharing the exact same weight matrices, exactly the visualization technique already covered as this topic's own core idea.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Unrolling draws one copy of the recurrent step for each time step, laid out in a line.
It transforms the compact, looping recurrent connection into a linear, easy-to-trace diagram.
Every unrolled copy shares the exact same weights; unrolling is purely a visual technique.
An unrolled Recurrent Neural Network becomes a specific kind of computational graph.
A longer sequence produces a longer unrolled graph, with more copies of the network.
Storing every unrolled copy's intermediate values costs more memory for longer sequences.
It is a necessary prerequisite for understanding Backpropagation Through Time.
Next up: Backpropagation Through Time, applying standard Backpropagation across this entire unrolled structure.
